sections.h2: How homeowners in St. Charles usually sell
sections.html:
Most use one of three paths: a listing through a broker, a sale they run themselves, or a cash purchase with no repairs requested. Repair needs and how rigid your timeline is usually decide it.

  • Broker listing: suits an updated house and an owner who can host showings for several weeks.
  • Owner-run sale: saves the agent's commission but puts pricing, marketing and negotiation on you.
  • Cash buyer: closes without loan approval, which helps with inherited houses, tenants in place or a pending relocation.

St. Charles homes tend to sell on location and condition. If yours has an open permit, an unfinished project or deferred maintenance, sort that out first, because open permits can hold up a sale.

sections.h2: St. Charles prices and long-time owners
sections.html:
St. Charles has an estimated 33,594 residents and 13,161 households. About 70.3% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the median home value is $377,400. Median gross rent is $1,819 and median household income is $114,300. Owner cost runs $2,381 a month with a mortgage and $1,102 without one.

Long tenure and an older age profile mean estate sales are a regular part of the local market. Buyers often compare a house near the river or the downtown grid with nearby Geneva and Batavia, so be ready to explain what sets your block apart. Families ask about schools early. St. Charles Community Unit School District 303 runs the public schools, so get your attendance zone from the district, not from a neighbor.

Take permit questions to the Building Division on the ground floor of City Hall, 2 E. Main Street, or call (630) 377-4406. The city says open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and that a disapproved final inspection means the work must be corrected before the sale.

Which projects need a St. Charles permit
ProjectPermit needed?
New or replacement fenceYes, and the plat of survey must show its location
Patios, decks, pools, flatwork, air conditioners, water heatersYes, with inspection
Electric service and panel workYes, plus an electric service application
Painting, wallpaper, flooring, cabinets, countertops, appliance swapsNo, if there is no electrical or plumbing change

The city runs its own electric utility, which is why electrical permits include a service application. Work done without a permit can be charged double fees once you apply, and a citation with an adjudication hearing is possible if you wait too long.

sections.h2: Plat of survey and city limits
sections.html:
A plat of survey submitted with a permit application must be 11 by 17 inches. If you lost yours, the Building Division can check its files.

Many homes carry a St. Charles mailing address but sit outside city limits. A letter in the numeric address, such as 12N123, signals unincorporated Kane County, where permits come from the county. St. Charles lies in both Kane and DuPage counties, so confirm which county holds your parcel number.

sections.h2: Why a St. Charles tax bill can rise
sections.html:
For a Kane County parcel, a township assessor sets the first value and the Supervisor of Assessments equalizes it. A DuPage County parcel goes through DuPage offices instead.

A bill can rise even when a value does not. Your exemptions may be incomplete, neighbors may qualify for exemptions you lack, taxing bodies may have raised levies, or your value may have moved faster than the neighborhood average. The largest share of a bill goes to schools, and the county cannot set another government's levy. The Property Tax Extension Limitation Law applies in Kane and generally caps levy increases at 5 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower. New construction, bonded debt and voter-approved increases fall outside that cap.

Complaints for a given year go to the Kane County Board of Review within 30 days of the township roll being published, and a bill that has already arrived is too late unless a complaint was filed. You can look at the township assessor's records for any parcel, including your own, to see how neighbors are valued. Your parcel number appears on your tax bill and your assessment notice. If your parcel's taxes were sold, redeem them at the County Clerk's tax extension office, 630-232-5964.

sections.h2: What is filed and taxed at closing
sections.html:
Your deed is filed in whichever county contains the parcel, and the title company usually handles the filing. State law prices the transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, paid with revenue stamps from the recorder, and a MyDec report goes to the Department of Revenue.

The county's share, the recording fee and any city requirement are separate questions. Ask the Kane County Recorder, or the DuPage County Recorder for a DuPage parcel, and ask City Hall whether a final read is needed on a water or electric account. The settlement statement will show every charge.

sections.h2: A cash sale in St. Charles without surprises
sections.html: A cash buyer takes the house without asking for repairs and without waiting on loan approval, so the work left is mostly paper. Close out open permits, confirm the county, locate your survey, and ask the city about the electric and water accounts. Then agree the price, the closing date and who pays each recording cost in the contract. A listing may bring more on a well-kept house, but a cash sale gives you a firm date and fewer showings.

faqs.q: Will an open permit delay my St. Charles closing?
faqs.a: It can. The city states that open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and unfinished or failed work must be corrected before the transfer.

faqs.q: Is my St. Charles address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. If the numeric address contains a letter, such as 12N123, the property is in unincorporated Kane County and permits come from the county.

faqs.q: Can I protest my St. Charles assessment after the tax bill arrives?
faqs.a: Generally no. Complaints for a given year must go to the Board of Review within 30 days of the township roll being published, and a bill that has already arrived is too late unless a complaint was filed.

faqs.q: Who handles electric service when a St. Charles house changes hands?
faqs.a: The city operates its own electric utility. Ask the city about the account transfer for your address.

faqs.q: What do I need for a fence permit?
faqs.a: A permit is required for a new or replacement fence, and the plat of survey must show where it sits. Submitted surveys must be 11 by 17 inches.
